en.title: Minimum Inversions When Merging Two Strings in Their Internal Order
en.description:
Merge two lowercase strings while keeping the internal relative order of each original string, and minimize the number of pairs i<j in the merged string with s[i]>s[j]. Inversions within the same original string also count; equal characters do not.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The two lines contain primary and secondary; the original bounds are 1≤length≤1000 for both, with lowercase letters only.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 2, 1 and 0. The second example can be merged into adadde. Counting only cross-string inversions, as the source does, would undercount the first example as 1; the adddae shown in the source is also not an optimal arrangement for the second example.
hints: For each letter, precompute for both strings the number of strictly greater characters in every prefix. dp[i][j] is the minimum number of inversions after merging the first i and j characters; appending the next character of either string adds the total number of strictly greater characters in the two used prefixes. Solve it with rolling rows.
